[ASSISTANT_SAID] Yes, you can definitely use color blocking techniques in your home decor.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips for creating a cohesive look with different shades of the same color include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Choose a color palette: Select a single color and choose a few shades.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Create contrast: Use different shades to create contrast and interest.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Use different textures and patterns: Add interest with various textures in the same color family.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Use a neutral base: Use neutral colors for walls and large furniture to highlight the chosen color.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Play with lighting: Experiment with lighting to see how colors look in different conditions.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Examples of textures that work well with color blocking techniques include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Velvets: Adds a luxurious texture, especially in jewel tones.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Linen: Adds a relaxed feel, works well with earthy colors.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Knits: Chunky knit throws and pillows add coziness.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Leather: Adds a rich texture, works well in warmer shades.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Woven textiles: Adds a natural feel, works well with deep earthy colors.
